root_motivation: Three sibling PRDs sharing `build_into: /home/jsy/wintermute/mcphost` this build cycle (`grand-loop-billing`, `mcphost-ci-sandbox-coverage`, `mcphost-metered-overage`) all ran `extend-gate.sh` at unchanged HEADs and got an identical `rollback-plan: block` naming the same five commits (`255cf1e`, `c0ed989`, `7297aee`, `04818b5`, plus a pre-existing `2da9b55`) as not individually `git-revert`-clean. Each PRD's own tick correctly attributed the block to shared repo/integration-chain state, not to its own diff, and correctly declined to force a pass — but nothing in the fleet resolves the underlying misclassification, so every future PRD touching mcphost hits the same wall until a human intervenes.
user_persona: The autobuilder skill orchestrator (a Claude session) and the human invoking `/autobuilder` from their own project. Both shell out to this binary for the receipt + gate steps that must not live in bash.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given `mcphost` has `agent/deploy-manifest.toml` present, When `rollback-plan` runs at the current `origin/main` HEAD, Then `resolve_rollback_model` returns `RedeployTag` and the receipt's `verdict` is `pass` (tag lineage check, not per-commit revert-clean).

Given the same repo and HEAD as AC1, When `extend-gate.sh /home/jsy/wintermute/mcphost --head <HEAD>` runs the full 25-receipt gate, Then `rollback-plan` is no longer in the blocking set (other pre-existing blockers named in the current `grand-loop-billing`/`mcphost-ci-sandbox-coverage` manifest entries — `vti-plan`, `reviewer-agent`'s history-not-revert-clean reason — may still need their own fix, but must not still cite rollback-plan).

Given a repo with no `agent/deploy-manifest.toml` and no explicit `rollback_model` (e.g. `summa`, `rustbuild`), When `rollback-plan` runs, Then it still resolves to `RevertCommits` (unchanged default) — regression test proving this PRD does not weaken the check fleet-wide.

Given a developer runs `autobuilder --help` or `rollback-plan --explain` (or reads the doc comment on `resolve_rollback_model`), When they look for `agent/deploy-manifest.toml`'s schema (even if fields beyond existence are still unused by `rollback.rs`), Then they find both `rollback_model` values enumerated with a one-line description of when each applies, documented in exactly one place.

Given mcphost's real `agent/intent-card.json`, When a helper (new script or `intent-card-refresh.sh` flag) runs against it, Then `rollback_model: redeploy-tag` is set idempotently (a second run makes no further change).

Given `wm-node` and `adopt`, When they are evaluated (not necessarily onboarded) against the same deploy-tag-or-not question, Then the finding is recorded in this PRD's own iter log rather than silently assumed.

scope: Stage 4 risk gate (7 receipts + release receipt)
non_goals: Spawning Claude subagents from the binary itself (that is the orchestrator's job)
Web-service, WASM, or embedded scaffolding (v1 supports cli + lib only)
Auto-applying self-evolution proposals (always gated for user review)
Re-running the underlying audit/test commands inside `gate` (gate only attests; producers own the work)

five_whys_trace.q: Why a Rust companion binary instead of a pure-skill scaffold?
five_whys_trace.a: Shell is too easy to subvert (set -e off, grep eaten, jq missing). The load-bearing parts — metric extraction, digest binding, schema validation — need a typed implementation under tests.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a 7-receipt gate instead of `cargo test && cargo clippy`?
five_whys_trace.a: Each receipt covers a class of failure that the others miss: clippy doesn't see CI status, tests don't see proof-lane routing, and none of them produce an independent-review record. The gate is what makes 'ready' falsifiable.

five_whys_trace.q: Why bootstrap autobuilder against itself before running it on other projects?
five_whys_trace.a: If the gate model can't certify the binary that produces gate receipts, it can't be trusted on any other project. The meta-bootstrap is the cheapest adversarial test of the whole pipeline.

five_whys_trace.q: Why deny unwrap/expect everywhere in src/ when most of this is glue code?
five_whys_trace.a: Glue code that panics on a missing receipt or malformed JSON destroys the audit trail at exactly the moments the gate matters most. Erroring back to the caller keeps the diagnostic surface alive.

five_whys_trace.q: Why digest-bind every receipt instead of trusting file timestamps?
five_whys_trace.a: Timestamps lie under git checkout. A self-binding sha256 lets the gate detect tampering and lets reviewers re-verify by recomputing on the receipt's own contents.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Where does the autobuilder repo's 'project' live for the gate — repo root or autobuilder/ workspace?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Repo root. agent/, scripts/, target/autobuilder/ all sit at /home/jsy/projects/autobuilder/. Proof-lanes globs use autobuilder/src/** prefix to match `git diff` output.
